title.narrative: Rural Water Supply, Sanitation, and Hygiene Improvement Sector Development Program

description.narrative:
The program will be aligned with the following impact: ensure availability and sustainability management of water and sanitation for all (Cambodia Sustainable Development Goal 6). The outcome will be improved access to safely managed and affordable drinking water, sanitation services and hygiene facilities for rural areas in nine project provinces. A sector development program, consisting of an investment loan (project component) and a policy-based loan (program component) is the most appropriate modality, given the critical policy actions required to further strengthen the ongoing sector reforms, and to compliment the government's commitment to expanding RWSS access and services to ensure that rural water supply, sanitation and hygiene development targets are met. The proposed reforms will include actions to cope with potential future development and growth, while leveraging difficult and critical water sector reforms, improve interministerial and/or interinstitutional coordination in the WASH sector.
The project component will expand RWSS access in at least 18 districts in 9 provinces, benefiting about 580,000 people. The project is expected to use a sector lending approach. RGC proposed that the following provinces are to be covered under the project component: (i) Banteay Meanchey, (ii) Battambang, (iii) Kampong Speu, (iv) Kampot, (v) Kratie, (vi) Otdar Meanchey, (vii) Pailin, (viii) Preah Vihear and (ix) Stung Treng. The program will be formulated to cover policy reforms to address among others: (i) inequalities to rural WASH services, (ii) inadequate operation and maintenance and the absence of tariff setting guidance, (iii) limited capacities of subnational administration to plan and deliver WASH services, and (iv) unclear mandate and limited interministerial/interinstitutional coordination and collaboration.

Output: Climate-resilient, inclusive, and safely managed rural sanitation and hygiene facilities improved and expanded. Indicator: At least 100 public schools and 10 community health centers in participating provinces provided with improved sanitation facilities that are climate-resilient and gender-inclusive and incorporate universal design principles Progress/Status: As of 31 December 2025: On-track. Under Batch 1: 40 schools will be provided with improved sanitation facilities that are climate-resilient and gender-inclusive and incorporate universal design principles. 1 latrine has been completed, and 21 latrines are under completion.
Under Batch 2, 58 schools and 13 health centers have been proposed for provision of improved sanitation facilities.
Data Source: District and commune council database, quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate-resilient, inclusive, and safely managed rural sanitation and hygiene facilities improved and expanded. Indicator: At least 4,100 climate-resilient, socially inclusive household latrines that incorporate universal design principles constructed in participating provinces Progress/Status: As of 31 December 2025: On-track. Batch 1: 1,242 HH latrines including 97 for HHs with PWDs and 366 for FHHs with ID Poor 1 • Two types of household latrines have been designed and constructed: one adapted for households with persons with disabilities (PWDs) and another for households without PWDs, to ensure accessibility and inclusiveness • HH latrines (for HHs without PWD) :21% • HH latrines for HHs with PWDs: 16.5% • HHLs have been designed and constructed with due consideration of flood risks, ensuring that key structures and components are elevated or protected to remain functional during flooding events. • Gender inclusion features (orientation will be provided to beneficiary HHs) include: • Full-height doors with internal locks for privacy and safety • Availability of water supply for hygiene, MHM, and comfort for women and girls • Tap or bucket for cleansing and washing • Soap near Latrine • Covered container for menstrual waste
Under Batch 2: 2001 ordinary HH latrines and 363 HH latrines that are disability friendly have been proposed.
Data Source: District and commune council database, quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate-resilient, inclusive, and safely managed rural water supply facilities improved and expanded. Indicator: SOP approved and implemented to mainstream climate change considerations, affordability, and inclusiveness principles in safely managed rural water supply investment Progress/Status: The SOP was approved in 2024. All SOPs and guidelines were approved and signed by the minister of rural development. The MRD confirmed that these SOPs and guidelines are binding to subnational administrations and can be considered similar to regulations in other countries. The government also confirmed that all SOPs and guidelines will be adopted and implemented nationwide in other WASH investments, aside from their implementation under the project component. The SOPs and guidelines will be referred to in the upcoming National Strategic Plan for Rural Water Supply, Sanitation, and Hygiene as requirements that should be complied with in rural WASH investment in Cambodia.
